findings.source: operate: LIQUIDITY.operate(token, supplyAmt, borrowAmt, withdrawTo, borrowTo, abi.encode(msg.sender)) (main.sol, the liquidity layer calls)
findings.issue: Each Liquidity operate call is built at mem[64] right after 'mem[64] = mem[64] + 64', yet the call reads 'mem[mem[64] len ...]' with mem[64] unresolved, and the bytes argument is copied by a word loop, so the six calls show neither function nor arguments.
findings.rule: Fold mem[64] to the value just stored to it (no intervening store to slot 64) and turn the word-wise copy of a bytes buffer into a copy line; the buffer then decodes as operate(...) with its bytes argument.

findings.source: liquidate's LiquidateMemoryVars / operate's OperateMemoryVars structs (tick, tickId, branch ids held in memory) used as mapping keys (_tickData[tick], _branchData[branchId], ...)
findings.issue: The memory structs that hold the current tick/branch are never turned into variables, so mapping keys are one-element concats of memory words (P4) and values are memory slices at pointer-arithmetic addresses (P14).
findings.rule: Promote memory words written at fixed offsets of a fresh allocation and only read back as scalars to SSA variables; a mapping key read from such a word is then the variable (m[k]) rather than concat(mem[..]).

findings.function: LIQUIDITY(), VAULT_FACTORY(), VAULT_ID(), constantsView() and all Liquidity calls
findings.source: ConstantVariables immutables (LIQUIDITY, VAULT_FACTORY, VAULT_ID, supply/borrow tokens, slots)
findings.issue: solc immutables read as 0 in pre-deployment code; Liquidity calls go to address 0. Not a decompiler error.

notes: 4 source loops, all whiles: Helpers.fetchLatestPosition:184 'while ((branchData_ & 3) == 2)' shown as 'while t % 4 == 2' (fetchLatestPosition and operate), liquidate:888 and its inner :946 'while (true)' (1006, 1027, with their breaks/continues), Helpers._fetchNextTopTick:299 'while (true)' (operate 1989). The other whiles are implicit: the word-loop copy of the abi.encode(msg.sender) bytes argument for the Liquidity calls (P7, 7 in operate, 1 in liquidate) and the event encoding. liquidate (1390 lines) and operate (2340 lines) reviewed by structure: tick/branch walks, packed storage updates (Fluid packs its storage by hand in the source, so whole-slot shift/mask writes are faithful, not P15), Liquidity calls, custom-error reverts (0x60121cca with error ids), events. No semantic error found.
summary: Faithful, with all four source loops shown as whiles; readability is limited by the hand-packed storage arithmetic (as in the source), memory-struct locals used as mapping keys, and Liquidity calls that lose their function and arguments.
